record.title: Kahn and Kalai's dense-subcube conjecture
record.statement:
Let $A\subset\{0,1\}^n$ be monotone increasing, with measure $\alpha=|A|/2^n\leq 1/2$. Its edge-boundary is denoted by $\partial A$. **Kahn and Kalai's conjecture.** For every $L>0$, there exist $L'>0$ and $\delta>0$ such that if

$$
|\partial A|\leq L|A|\log_2(2^n/|A|),
$$

then there is a subcube $C\subset\{0,1\}^n$ of measure at least $\alpha^{L'}$, with all fixed coordinates equal to $1$, such that

$$
\frac{|A\cap C|}{|C|}\geq(1+\delta)\alpha.
$$

The hypothesis requires the boundary to be within a constant factor of the edge-isoperimetric minimum, while the conclusion finds a fairly large subcube on which the density increases by a constant factor. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Itai Benjamini, David Ellis, Ehud Friedgut, Nathan Keller and Arnab Sen, “Juntas in the ^1-grid and Lipschitz maps between discrete tori”, arXiv:1311.6958 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.6958

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).

record.title: Universal-building category conjecture for semisimple Hitchin systems
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a semisimple complex Lie group, let $X$ be a Riemann surface, and let

$$
\phi\in\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}H^0(X,\omega_X^{\otimes d_i})
$$

be a point in the corresponding Hitchin base. Let $h^{\phi}$ be the harmonic map to the universal building associated to $\phi$. **Universal-building category conjecture.** The singularities of $h^{\phi}$ determine a $3$-dimensional Calabi--Yau category $\mathcal C$. The paper presents this as an expected extension from the $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb C)$ case to arbitrary semisimple Lie groups. It gives initial evidence but no general construction or proof.
record.source_name: Ludmil Katzarkov, Alexander Noll, Pranav Pandit and Carlos Simpson, “Harmonic Maps to Buildings and Singular Perturbation Theory”, arXiv:1311.7101 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.7101

record.title: The filling pair systole lower-bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $S_g$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g$, let $\mathcal{M}_g$ denote its moduli space of hyperbolic metrics, and let $m_g$ be the minimum perimeter of a regular, right-angled $(8g-4)$-gon. Define $\mathcal{Y}_g:\mathcal{M}_g\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ to be the **filling pair systole** function, which assigns to each hyperbolic metric the length of the shortest filling pair. **Filling pair systole conjecture.** For every hyperbolic metric in $\mathcal{M}_g$, one has

$$
\mathcal{Y}_g\geq m_g/2.
$$

This conjecture extends the lower bound established in the paper for filling pairs whose complement has at most two regions; it predicts the same universal lower bound for the shortest filling pair in general.
record.source_name: Tarik Aougab and Shinnyih Huang, “Minimally intersecting filling pairs on surfaces”, arXiv:1312.0913 (2013).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.0913

record.title: Ryan–Pomerance conjecture on maximal heights for $pq^b$
record.statement:
Let $p<q$ be odd primes, and define

$$
B(n):=\max\{H(f): f\mid x^n-1,\ f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]\},
$$

where $H(f)$ is the largest absolute value of a coefficient of $f$. **Ryan–Pomerance height conjecture.** For every positive integer $b$,

$$
B(2q^b)=2,
$$

and for every positive integer $b>2$,

$$
B(pq^b)>p.
$$

These are further conjectures attributed in the source to Ryan and collaborators. They refine known calculations such as $B(pq)=\min\{p,q\}$ and $B(pq^2)=\min\{p,q^2\}$, while the excerpt gives no resolution of the two assertions.
record.source_name: Shaozu Wang, “Maximal height of divisors of x^pq^b-1”, arXiv:1312.3108 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3108

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: Jablan–Sazdanović conjecture on unknotting numbers of positive odd pretzel knots
record.statement:
Let $P(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ be the pretzel knot with $n$ odd and positive odd integers $a_1,\dots,a_n$, ordered so that $a_1\leq a_2\leq\dots\leq a_n$. **Jablan–Sazdanović conjecture.**

$$
u(P(a_1,\dots,a_n))=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i}{2}.
$$

This conjecture would determine the unknotting number for all pretzel knots with an odd number of positive odd parameters. The paper proves special cases, including families with parameters $(3,1,\dots,1,b)$ and $(3a,3b,3c)$, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Seph Shewell Brockway, “Computing the unknotting numbers of certain pretzel knots”, arXiv:1312.4502 (2013).

record.title: Conjecture on Dickson-polynomial auxiliary functions for CPP exponents
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $r+1$ be a prime with $r+1\neq p$, assume $\gcd(r,k)=1$ and $\gcd(r+1,p^2-1)=1$, and set

$$
d=\frac{p^{rk}-1}{p^k-1}+1.
$$
The functions $h_a(x)$ are associated to elements $a\in\mathbb{F}_{p^{rk}}^*$.

**Dickson-polynomial conjecture.** There exist $a\in\mathbb{F}_{p^{rk}}^*$ such that $h_a(x)$ are Dickson polynomials of degree $r+1$ over $\mathbb{F}_{p^k}$.

This conjecture concerns a family of exponents used to construct complete permutation polynomials. It has been proved for several parameter choices, including $p=2$ with $r=4,6,10$, $p=3$ with $r=4,6$, and $p=5$ with $r=6$; it was also verified computationally for $p=3$, $r=10$, and $1\leq k\leq 3$.
record.source_name: Gaofei Wu, Nian Li, Tor Helleseth and Yuqing Zhang, “More Classes of Complete Permutation Polynomials over _q”, arXiv:1312.4716 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.4716

record.title: Erdős–Tuza conjecture on $K_4$-saturating edges
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex $K_4$-free graph. An edge in $\overline{G}$ is **$K_4$-saturating** if adding it to $G$ creates a copy of $K_4$. Let $f(n,e)$ be the maximum integer $\ell$ such that every $n$-vertex $K_4$-free graph with $e$ edges has at least $\ell$ $K_4$-saturating edges.

**Erdős–Tuza conjecture.**

$$
f(n,\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1)=(1+o(1))\frac{n^2}{16}.
$$

Equivalently, every $n$-vertex $K_4$-free graph with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1$ edges has at least $(1+o(1))n^2/16$ $K_4$-saturating edges. This is an Erdős–Rademacher-type extremal problem: adding one edge beyond the Turán bound for $K_4$-free graphs should force quadratically many saturating non-edges. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
record.source_name: József Balogh and Hong Liu, “On the number of K_4-saturating edges”, arXiv:1312.5248 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.5248

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

record.title: McKay–Wanless conjecture on near-quadratic automorphism orders of quasigroups
record.statement:
Let $f(n)$ denote the maximum of the orders of automorphisms of quasigroups of order at most $n$. The preceding discussion gives $f(n)=O(n^2)$. **McKay–Wanless conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$ and for infinitely many values of $n$,

$$
f(n)>n^{2-\epsilon}.
$$

This conjecture says that the exponent $2$ in the quadratic upper bound is best possible in the sense that values of $f(n)$ come arbitrarily close to $n^2$ along an infinite sequence. The source attributes it to McKay et al.; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: László Babai and Ákos Seress, “Element order versus minimal degree in permutation groups: an old lemma with new applications”, arXiv:1401.0489 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0489

record.title: Cilleruelo's lower-bound conjecture for infinite $C_4$-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $\epsilon>0$. A countable infinite graph with no cycle of length four is called $C_4$-free, and let $\mathcal{G}_n$ denote the subgraph induced by the first $n$ vertices. Write $\delta(\mathcal{G}_n)$ for its minimum degree. **Cilleruelo's conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, there exists a countable infinite $C_4$-free graph $\mathcal{G}$ such that

$$
\delta(\mathcal{G}_n)\gg n^{1/2-\epsilon}.
$$

This conjecture proposes that, despite the obstruction posed by extending finite algebraic constructions to infinite graphs, infinite $C_4$-free graphs can still have minimum degree close to the finite-graph scale $\sqrt n$.
record.source_name: Javier Cilleruelo, “Infinite graphs that do not contain cycles of length four”, arXiv:1401.4502 (2016).

record.title: Diagonalizability of adjoint-abelian operators in smooth Minkowski spaces
record.statement:
Let a **smooth Minkowski space** be a finite-dimensional real normed space whose norm is smooth away from the origin, and let an **adjoint-abelian operator** be a linear operator $A$ satisfying

$$
[Ax,y]=[x,Ay]
$$

for all vectors $x,y$, where $[\cdot,\cdot]$ denotes the semi-inner product associated with the norm. **Diagonalizability conjecture.** Every adjoint-abelian operator of a smooth Minkowski space is diagonalizable. The source presents this as a consequence of a cited theorem, so the claim may already be resolved; the supplied parser status does not determine its resolution.
record.source_name: Ákos G. Horváth, “Isometries of Minkowski geometries”, arXiv:1401.4898 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.4898

record.title: The minimum-degree lower-bound conjecture for H-free subgraphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of graphs, and let $h(\delta,\Delta,\mathcal{F})$ be the minimum, over graphs $G$ with minimum degree $\delta$ and maximum degree $\Delta$, of the largest minimum degree of an $\mathcal{F}$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. Let $\operatorname{ex}(K_\Delta,\mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $\mathcal{F}$-free subgraph of the complete graph $K_\Delta$.
**Minimum-degree lower-bound conjecture.** For every $\delta$, $\Delta$ and every family $\mathcal{F}$,

$$
h(\delta,\Delta,\mathcal{F})=\Omega\left(\frac{\operatorname{ex}(K_\Delta,\mathcal{F})\delta}{\Delta^2}\right).
$$

The conjecture would remove the logarithmic loss in the paper's general lower bound for $h$. The source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Florent Foucaud, Michael Krivelevich and Guillem Perarnau, “Large subgraphs without short cycles”, arXiv:1401.4928 (2014).

record.title: Lagarias–Soundararajan's strong XYZ conjecture for ABC solutions
record.statement:
Let $\frak X$ be the set of primitive nonzero integer solutions $(A,B,C)$ to $A+B+C=0$, and define

$$
H(A,B,C)=\max\{|A|,|B|,|C|\},\qquad S(A,B,C)=P^+(ABC),
$$

where $P^+(n)$ is the largest prime divisor of $n$.

**XYZ conjecture (strong form).** For every $\epsilon>0$, both of the following hold:

(a) only finitely many $(A,B,C)\in\frak X$ satisfy

$$
\log H(A,B,C)>S(A,B,C)^{2/3+\epsilon};
$$

(b) infinitely many $(A,B,C)\in\frak X$ satisfy

$$
\log H(A,B,C)>S(A,B,C)^{2/3-\epsilon}.
$$

This conjecture relates the height of an ABC solution to the largest prime factor of its product. The text says that the ABC conjecture implies a weaker version of part (a), with exponent $1+\epsilon$, while the stated exponent $2/3+\epsilon$ is not known to follow from ABC.
record.source_name: James E. Weigandt, “Insulators of ABC Solutions”, arXiv:1401.6439 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.6439

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: Midpoint-minimum conjecture for the Bernstein basis square-sum
record.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the Bernstein operator with basis polynomials $b_{nk}(x)=\binom{n}{k}x^k(1-x)^{n-k}$, and define

$$
\varphi_n(x):=\sum_{k=0}^{n}b_{nk}^2(x),\qquad x\in[0,1].
$$

**Midpoint-minimum conjecture.** For every $x\in[0,1]$,

$$
\varphi_n(x)\geq\varphi_n\left(\frac12\right).
$$

This asserts that the midpoint is a global minimizer of the Bernstein basis square-sum and is implied by the preceding monotonicity claim; the source states it as another conjecture and supplies no resolution.
record.source_name: Heiner Gonska, Ioan Raşa and Maria-Daniela Rusu, “Chebyshev-Grüss-type inequalities via discrete oscillations”, arXiv:1401.7908 (2014).

record.title: Computational hardness of submatrix localization below the convexified MLE threshold
record.statement:
Let $Y^*$ denote the true support matrix in the submatrix localization model. Assume $\mu\le 1$, $n_L=n_R=n$, $K_L=K_R=K$, and $K\ge c_1\log n$. **Submatrix localization computational-hardness conjecture.** For every constant $\epsilon>0$, no algorithm with running time polynomial in $n$ can, for all $n$ and with probability at least $1/2$, output $Y^*$ when

$$
\mu^2\le\frac{n^{1-\epsilon}}{K^2}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that no polynomial-time method substantially improves on the convexified maximum-likelihood estimator, whose recovery boundary is $\mu^2\asymp n/K^2$ up to logarithmic factors; the conjectured gap from the minimax boundary remains open.
record.source_name: Yudong Chen and Jiaming Xu, “Statistical-Computational Tradeoffs in Planted Problems and Submatrix Localization with a Growing Number of Clusters and Submatrices”, arXiv:1402.1267 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.1267

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The $j_1$ criterion for regular sequences
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an ${\bf R}$-module satisfying a condition (C), and let $\mathbf{x}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_r\}$ be a partial system of parameters for $M$. Set $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathbf{x}}(M)$ for the associated graded module and let $j_1(\mathbf{x};M)$ be its first generalized Hilbert coefficient.

**$j_1$ regular-sequence conjecture.** If

$$
\dim \mathrm{H}^0_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathbf{x}}(M))=r
\quad\text{and}\quad
j_1(\mathbf{x};M)=0,
$$

then $\mathbf{x}$ is a regular sequence on $M$. The condition (C) is not fixed in the source; at minimum, $M$ should be unmixed. The source also describes a weak version in which the vanishing is assumed for all partial systems of parameters of $r$ elements. The status is not specified.
record.source_name: Wolmer V. Vasconcelos, “Complexity Degrees of Algebraic Structures”, arXiv:1402.1906 (2014).

record.title: The magic-number conjecture for strong cyclotomic Delone sets
record.statement: Let $n\ge 3$, let $N=[n,2]$, and let $m_n$ denote the minimum number of pairwise nonparallel $\varLambda$-directions whose X-rays determine every convex subset of a strong $n$-cyclotomic Delone set $\varLambda$. **Magic-number conjecture.** With the exception of $m_4=7$, the trivial lower bound $m_n=N+1$ is the magic number for strong $n$-cyclotomic Delone sets for all $n\ge 3$. The exception reflects the affine equivalence of the triangular and square lattice cases, for which six lattice directions can contain a $U$-polygon.
record.source_name: Christian Huck, Markus Moll and Johan Nilsson, “Discrete tomography: Magic numbers for N-fold symmetry”, arXiv:1402.2183 (2014).

record.title: Rödl–Ruciński tight Hamilton-cycle conjecture for hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta_1(G)$ denote its minimum vertex degree. **Rödl–Ruciński conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is an integer $n_0$ such that, whenever $n\ge n_0$ and

$$
\delta_1(G)\ge\left(1-\left(1-\frac1k\right)^{k-1}+\varepsilon\right)\binom{n}{k-1},
$$

$G$ contains a tight Hamilton cycle. The conjecture is wide open; the preceding results concern codegree conditions rather than vertex-degree conditions.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Hamilton cycles in graphs and hypergraphs: an extremal perspective”, arXiv:1402.4268 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.4268

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

record.title: The diffeomorphism conjecture for the 16- and 17-vertex triangulations of the K3 surface
record.statement:
Let $(K3)_{16}$ and $(K3)_{17}$ denote the 16-vertex and 17-vertex triangulations, respectively, of the K3 surface. **K3 triangulation diffeomorphism conjecture.**

$$
(K3)_{16}\text{ and }(K3)_{17}\text{ are diffeomorphic}.
$$

The smooth type of $(K3)_{17}$ is canonical, whereas the smooth type of $(K3)_{16}$ was unknown in the source context. Since piecewise-linear and smooth manifolds correspond in dimension four, resolving this conjecture would determine whether these two triangulations represent the same smooth 4-manifold.
record.source_name: Benjamin A. Burton and Jonathan Spreer, “Computationally proving triangulated 4-manifolds to be diffeomorphic”, arXiv:1403.2780 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.2780

record.title: Strong equitable vertex arboricity bounded by maximum degree
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, and let $a^*_{eq}(G)$ be the smallest integer $t$ such that $G$ has an equitable $t'$-tree-coloring for every $t'\geq t$, where an equitable $k$-tree-coloring is a partition of $V(G)$ into $k$ parts whose sizes differ by at most one and each part induces a forest. **Strong equitable vertex arboricity conjecture.**

$$
a^*_{eq}(G)\leq \left\lceil\frac{\Delta(G)+1}{2}\right\rceil
$$

This conjecture proposes a maximum-degree bound for the strong equitable vertex arboricity of every graph. Its resolution is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Xin Zhang, “Equitable vertex arboricity of planar graphs”, arXiv:1403.2810 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.2810

record.title: Complex Gr"unbaum lower-bound conjecture for regular fans
record.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, let $k\geq 1$, and let $q_1,\ldots,q_k>2$ be integers. Set

$$
Q=\prod_{j=1}^k q_j.
$$

Here $\Delta_{\mathbb{C}}(m;q_1,\ldots,q_k)$ is the minimum dimension $d$ such that any $m$ measures on $\mathbb{C}^d$ can be equipartitioned by $Q$ regions determined by $k$ complex regular $q_j$-fans. **Complex Gr"unbaum lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
k\Delta_{\mathbb{C}}(m;q_1,\ldots,q_k)\geq m\left\lfloor\frac{Q-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This conjecture extends the known lower bound for a single complex regular fan to arbitrary numbers of fans and is motivated by the moment-curve argument used in the real Gr"unbaum problem. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Steven Simon, “Measure Equipartitions via Finite Fourier Analysis”, arXiv:1403.7094 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7094

record.title: The exact online Ramsey number conjecture for paths
record.statement:
Let $P_m$ denote the path on $m$ vertices, and let $\tilde{r}(P_a,P_b)$ denote the online Ramsey number for the pair of graphs $P_a$ and $P_b$.

**Exact path Ramsey conjecture.** For all integers $\ell\ge 3$,

$$
\tilde{r}(P_4,P_{\ell+1})=\left\lceil\frac{7\ell+2}{5}\right\rceil.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes upper and lower bounds differing by an additive constant, and the lower bound is believed to be tight; the conjecture asserts the exact value.
record.source_name: Joanna Cyman, Tomasz Dzido, John Lapinskas and Allan Lo, “On-line Ramsey numbers of paths and cycles”, arXiv:1404.3894 (2014).

record.title: Stability conjecture for distinguishing newforms at squarefree level
record.statement: Let $n_0(N,k)$ be the smallest nonnegative integer such that, for any newforms $f,g\in S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$, equality $a_n(f)=a_n(g)$ for all $n\leq n_0(N,k)$ implies $f=g$. Let $N\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ be squarefree. **Stability conjecture.** There exists $K\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ such that if $k\geq K$ is an even integer, then $n_0(N,k)$ is equal to the least prime that does not divide $N$. This predicts that, for fixed squarefree level, the number of initial Fourier coefficients needed to distinguish newforms eventually stabilizes at the first prime not dividing the level.
record.source_name: Sam Chow and Alexandru Ghitza, “Distinguishing newforms”, arXiv:1404.4508 (2014).

record.title: Fiamčík's acyclic edge coloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, undirected graph, let $Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, and let $chi'_{a}(G)$ denote the least number of colors in a proper edge coloring of $G$ in which every cycle receives at least three colors.

**Acyclic edge coloring conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\chi'_{a}(G)\leq \Delta(G)+2.
$$

This conjecture, stated by Fiamčík in 1978 and restated by Alon et al. in 2001, is the central bound for the acyclic chromatic index; the supplied text does not establish whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Tao Wang and Yaqiong Zhang, “Further result on acyclic chromatic index of planar graphs”, arXiv:1405.0713 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.0713

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

record.title: Stable cohomology conjecture for finite p-groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group, and let $d$ be its stable cohomological dimension, namely the largest degree in which stable cohomology of $G$ is nonzero.

**Stable-cohomology top-degree conjecture.** There exists a $G$-module $A$ with trivial action such that

$$
H^d_{\mathrm{s}}(G,A)\neq 0.
$$

This asserts that the stable cohomological dimension of every finite $p$-group is attained using a trivial-coefficient module. The source provides no evidence of resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Fedor Bogomolov and Christian Böhning, “Essential dimension, stable cohomological dimension, and stable cohomology of finite Heisenberg groups”, arXiv:1405.1394 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.1394

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

record.title: Conjectured upper bound for the saturation number of fullerene graphs
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a fullerene graph on $n$ vertices, and let $s(F)$ denote its saturation number, the minimum cardinality of a maximal matching in $F$.

**Fullerene saturation-number conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that

$$
s(F)\leq \frac{n}{3}+C
$$

for every fullerene graph $F$ on $n$ vertices.

The preceding lower and upper bounds are asymptotically equal, but the exact value of the saturation number remains open. This conjecture asserts that the upper bound differs from $n/3$ by at most an absolute constant.
record.source_name: Vesna Andova, František Kardoš and Riste Škrekovski, “Sandwiching saturation number of fullerene graphs”, arXiv:1405.2197 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2197

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2014). “This conjecture was proven by Esperet et al. .”

record.title: Chirality conjecture for the $E_{2k+1}$ knot family
record.statement:
For each integer $k\geq 1$, let $E_{2k+1}$ denote the family of alternating knots that embed on an $M_{2k+1}$ mosaic with $|D|=2$, where $D$ is the relevant dual structure. A knot is **chiral** if it is not ambient isotopic to its mirror image. **Chirality conjecture for the $E_{2k+1}$ family.**

$$
E_{2k+1}\text{ knots are chiral.}
$$

The source motivates this from the non-palindromic Jones polynomial of the smallest member $7_{4}$, but does not establish chirality for every member of the family; the claim therefore remains open.
record.source_name: Hugh Howards and Andrew Kobin, “Crossing Number Bound in Knot Mosaics”, arXiv:1405.7683 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7683

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2014). “This was proven by Kuriya in , so as a result, we can treat knot equivalence and crossing number of knot mosaics in the usual way.”

record.title: The connected triangle-free Ramsey simplicity conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $H$, let $s(H)$ denote the minimum degree among all Ramsey $H$-minimal graphs, and let $\delta(H)$ denote the minimum degree of $H$. A graph $H$ is **Ramsey simple** when

$$
s(H)=2\delta(H)-1.
$$

**Connected triangle-free Ramsey simplicity conjecture.** For every connected triangle-free graph $H$ on at least $2$ vertices,

$$
s(H)=2\delta(H)-1.
$$

This is a strengthened, explicitly connected formulation of the triangle-free conjecture. The source states that it remains open; the equality is known for $3$-connected regular triangle-free graphs under an additional technical condition.
record.source_name: Andrey Grinshpun, Raj Raina and Rik Sengupta, “Minimum Degrees of Minimal Ramsey Graphs for Almost-Cliques”, arXiv:1406.6746 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.6746

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2014). “The conjecture of remains open.”

record.title: The Adams differential conjecture for the eta-local motivic sphere
record.statement:
Let $A$ be the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra, let $h_1$ denote the class corresponding to $\tau_0$, and let $v_k$ be the generators in the $h_1$-localized $\operatorname{Ext}_A$ algebra. The $2$-complete motivic Adams spectral sequence for the eta-local motivic sphere $S^{0,0}[eta^{-1}]$ has $E_2$-page $\operatorname{Ext}_A[h_1^{-1}]$. **Adams differential conjecture.** For all $k geq 3$, there is an Adams differential

$$
d_2(v_k)=h_1v_{k-1}^2.
$$

These differentials extend the known cases $d_2(v_3)=h_1v_2^2$ and $d_2(v_4)=h_1v_3^2$. Identifying all Adams differentials would determine the homotopy of the eta-local motivic sphere; the source expects these differentials but does not establish them in general.

record.title: Hansen and Zwick's Fibonacci conjecture for Order-Regular matrices
record.statement:
Let an **Order-Regular matrix** be a binary matrix satisfying the Order-Regularity constraints arising from Policy Iteration on cube acyclic Unique Sink Orientations. For an $n$-column Order-Regular matrix, let $F_k$ denote the $k$th Fibonacci number. **Hansen and Zwick's Fibonacci conjecture.** The maximum number of rows of an $n$-column Order-Regular matrix is given by $F_{n+2}$, the $(n+2)$nd Fibonacci number.

Hansen and Zwick proposed this conjecture after exhaustive searches for matrices with up to six columns, whose maximum row counts were $2,3,5,8,13,21$. The paper disproves the conjecture by constructing Order-Regular matrices exceeding the corresponding Fibonacci bounds.

record.title: The forbidden-matching avoidance conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a multigraph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ and maximum multiplicity $\mu(G)$. A **forbidden matching** is a matching whose edges have been assigned arbitrary, not necessarily proper, colours from a palette. **The forbidden-matching avoidance conjecture.** Using the palette $\mathcal{K}=[\Delta(G)+\mu(G)]$, any forbidden matching can be avoided by a proper edge-colouring of all of $G$, meaning that the colouring disagrees with the assigned colour on every forbidden edge. This is a significant weakening of the edge-precolouring extension conjecture and is not implied by the List Colouring Conjecture; its proof was left open in the paper.
record.source_name: Katherine Edwards, António Girão, Jan van den Heuvel, Ross J. Kang, Gregory J. Puleo and Jean-Sébastien Sereni, “Extension from Precoloured Sets of Edges”, arXiv:1407.4339 (2018).

record.title: Bellaterra graphs are two-sided expanders
record.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the $3$-regular Bellaterra graph at level $n$, for $n\geq 1$. A family of $3$-regular graphs is **two-sided expanding** when there is an $\varepsilon>0$ such that its second-largest and smallest eigenvalues satisfy

$$
\lambda_2<3-\varepsilon\qquad\text{and}\qquad\lambda_n>-3+\varepsilon.
$$

**Bellaterra expander conjecture.** The Bellaterra graphs $\{B_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ are a family of two-sided expanders. The authors' computations suggest an eigenvalue gap of roughly $0.05$, but the conjecture remains unproved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Anton Malyshev and Igor Pak, “Lifts, derandomization, and diameters of Schreier graphs of Mealy automata”, arXiv:1407.4600 (2014).

record.title: Modified maximum subset-divisor conjecture
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set of $n$ positive integers, let $d_k(A)$ be the number of $k$-subsets $B$ of $A$ satisfying $\sum B\mid\sum A$, and let $d(k,n)$ be the maximum of $d_k(A)$ over all such sets $A$. **Modified subset-divisor conjecture.** For all but finitely many integer pairs $(k,n)$ with $1<k<n$,

$$
d(k,n)=\binom{n-1}{k}.
$$

This is the paper's corrected form after excluding the infinite families of counterexamples to Huynh's formulation; the paper states that, apart from those families, the conjecture is true.
record.source_name: Samuel Zbarsky, “The Maximum Number of Subset Divisors of a Given Size”, arXiv:1407.4720 (2015).

record.title: The connected-graph bound for eternal connected domination
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, let $\theta(G)$ denote its clique covering number, and let $\gamma_c^{\infty}(G)$ denote its eternal connected domination number. **The eternal connected domination conjecture.** For every connected graph $G$ with

$$
\Delta(G)<n-1,
$$

one has

$$
\gamma_c^{\infty}(G)>\theta(G).
$$

The source lists this among open problems in the other eternal-protection models.
record.source_name: William F. Klostermeyer and Christina M. Mynhardt, “Protecting a Graph with Mobile Guards”, arXiv:1407.5228 (2015).

record.title: Distinct-prime Goldbach variation below the largest prime
record.statement:
Let $n\geqslant 12$ be an even integer, and let $p$ be the largest prime less than $n$. **Distinct-prime Goldbach variation.** There exist distinct primes $r$ and $s$ such that

$$
r<s<p\qquad\text{and}\qquad n=r+s.
$$

This number-theoretic assertion is introduced because it would control the prime-graph comparison in the special cases of alternating groups discussed in the paper. It is presented as an assumed variation of Goldbach's conjecture and remains open.
record.source_name: Timothy C. Burness and Elisa Covato, “On the prime graph of simple groups”, arXiv:1407.8128 (2014).

record.title: The $m(G)/17$ bound for induced matchings without $C_5^2$ components
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $m(G)$ denote its number of edges, and let $C_5^2$ denote the graph obtained by replacing each vertex of a $5$-cycle with an independent set of order $2$. An **induced matching** is a matching whose endpoints induce exactly the edges in the matching; write $
u_s(G)$ for the maximum size of an induced matching in $G$. **The $m(G)/17$ conjecture.** If $G$ has maximum degree at most $4$ and no component is isomorphic to $C_5^2$, then

$$
\nu_s(G)\geq \frac{m(G)}{17}.
$$

The preceding theorem gives the best possible general bound with a possible $C_5^2$ component, while the source notes that no example without such a component attaining the weaker ratio $m(G)/18$ was known. The proposed bound remains open in the paper.
record.source_name: Felix Joos, “Induced Matchings in Graphs of Maximum Degree 4”, arXiv:1407.8336 (2014).

record.title: Enomoto and Ota's path-partition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, let $k\geq 3$ be an integer, and let $n_{1},\dots,n_{k}$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_i=n.
$$

Write $\sigma_2(G)$ for the minimum degree sum of two nonadjacent vertices. **Enomoto and Ota's conjecture.** If

$$
\sigma_2(G)\geq n+k-1,
$$

then for any $k$ distinct vertices $x_1,\dots,x_k$ in $G$, there exist vertex-disjoint paths $P_1,\dots,P_k$ such that $|P_i|=n_i$ and $P_i$ starts at $x_i$ for every $1\leq i\leq k$. The conjecture predicts a prescribed path partition of the entire vertex set under a degree-sum condition; the paper proves it when the order of $G$ is sufficiently large, while the remaining cases are not addressed here.
record.source_name: Vincent Coll, Alexander Halperin, Colton Magnant and Pouria Salehi Nowbandegani, “Enomoto and Ota's conjecture holds for large graphs”, arXiv:1408.0408 (2014).

record.title: Hitting clause-sets attain the minimum variable-degree of minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets
record.statement:
For $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\operatorname{minnonmer}(k)$ be the minimum variable-degree over minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets of deficiency $k$, and let $\operatorname{minnonmerh}(k)$ be the corresponding quantity restricted to unsatisfiable hitting clause-sets. **Hitting-minimum-degree conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\operatorname{minnonmer}(k)=\operatorname{minnonmerh}(k).
$$

This asserts that the extremal examples determining the minimum are always available among unsatisfiable hitting clause-sets; the paper presents it as an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Oliver Kullmann and Xishun Zhao, “Bounds for variables with few occurrences in conjunctive normal forms”, arXiv:1408.0629 (2017).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.0629

record.title: Sharp lower bound for the minimum variable-degree of minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets
record.statement:
For $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\operatorname{minnonmer}(k)$ denote the minimum variable-degree among minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets of deficiency $k$, and let $\operatorname{nM}(k)$ be the non-Mersenne bound. **Sharpness conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\operatorname{minnonmer}(k)\ge \operatorname{nM}(k)-1.
$$

The paper notes that the exact function is complicated, but conjectures that it differs from the non-Mersenne bound by at most one; the statement remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Oliver Kullmann and Xishun Zhao, “Bounds for variables with few occurrences in conjunctive normal forms”, arXiv:1408.0629 (2017).

record.title: Full clauses attain the non-Mersenne lower bound up to one
record.statement:
For $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\operatorname{maxsmar}(k)$ be the maximum number of full clauses in a minimally unsatisfiable clause-set of deficiency $k$, and let $\operatorname{nM}(k)$ be the non-Mersenne bound. **Full-clause conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\operatorname{maxsmar}(k)\ge \operatorname{nM}(k)-1.
$$

The claim is motivated by numerical investigations showing that the maximum number of full clauses is close to the minimum variable-degree and to the non-Mersenne bound; no resolution is given.

record.title: The finite Turán threshold conjecture for posets
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset. For each $n$, let ${\rm La}^{*}(n,P)$ be the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ containing no induced copy of $P$, and define the induced Turán threshold by

$$
\pi^{*}(P)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{{\rm La}^{*}(n,P)}{\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}}.
$$

**Finite Turán threshold conjecture.** Every poset has a finite Turán threshold, that is, $\pi^{*}(P)<\infty$ for every finite poset $P$.

The paper proves finiteness for series-parallel posets and posets of height $2$. The conjecture asks for the corresponding result for arbitrary finite posets.
record.source_name: Linyuan Lu and Kevin G. Milans, “Set families with forbidden subposets”, arXiv:1408.0646 (2014).

record.title: The pre-colored leaf extension conjecture
record.statement: Let $f(k)$ be the smallest integer $f$ such that for every $d\in[k]$ the following holds. Let $G$ be an arbitrary finite graph such that every degree is at most $d$, except at most one vertex of degree $d+1$. Suppose that at most $d-1$ leaves, that is, edges with one of their endpoints having degree $1$, are pre-colored. Then this pre-coloring can be extended to an edge-coloring of the whole graph $G$ that uses at most $d+f$ different colors. **Pre-colored leaf extension conjecture.** $f(k)=1$ for all $k\geqslant 1$. This conjecture would strengthen Vizing's theorem by asserting that the specified pre-coloring can always be extended using only $d+1$ colors, even when one vertex has degree $d+1$.
record.source_name: Endre Csóka, Gabor Lippner and Oleg Pikhurko, “Kőnig's Line Coloring and Vizing's Theorems for Graphings”, arXiv:1408.1973 (2016).

record.title: Strong Terminating Conjecture for M&m sequences
record.statement: Starting from the normalized initial values $0<x<1$, let $(x_4,x_5,\ldots)$ be the associated M\&m sequence, and let $L(x)$ denote the minimum integer $k$ such that $x_n=x_k$ for all $n>k$. **Strong Terminating Conjecture.** For every $0<x<1$, there exists an integer $k$ such that $x_n=x_k$ for all $n>k$; equivalently, $L(x)<\infty$, or the associated sequence of medians eventually becomes constant. This is the normalized formulation of the stability conjecture. The paper's abstract says that the conjecture is proved for a subset of possible starting conditions, while the full statement remains open in the supplied source.

record.title: Lehel's strengthened Erdős–Gallai–Tuza conjecture
record.statement:
Given an $n$-vertex graph $G$, let $alpha_1(G)$ be the maximum size of a triangle-independent set of edges. Let $oldtau_{\mathrm{B}}(G)$ be the minimum size of an edge set $X$ such that $G-X$ is bipartite.

**Lehel's strengthened Erdős–Gallai–Tuza conjecture.** For every $n$-vertex graph $G$,

$$
\alpha_1(G)+\oldtau_{\mathrm{B}}(G)\leq \frac{n^2}{4}.
$$

This is a stronger variant because $oldtau_{\mathrm{B}}(G)\geq \oldtau_1(G)$. The source attributes it to Lehel and independently to the author, and does not state a resolution, so it is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Gregory J. Puleo, “Extremal Aspects of the Erdős–Gallai–Tuza Conjecture”, arXiv:1408.5176 (2015).

record.title: Extreme-point conjecture for Nikol'skii constants
record.statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a convex compact set, and let $C(\mathcal{P}_N,D,\boldsymbol{x})$ denote the Nikol'skii constant at $\boldsymbol{x}\in D$ for the polynomial space $\mathcal{P}_N$. An **extreme point** of $D$ is a point of $D$ that does not lie in any open line segment joining two points of $D$. **Extreme-point conjecture.** The maximum

$$
\max_{\boldsymbol{x}\in D} C(\mathcal{P}_N,D,\boldsymbol{x})
$$

is achieved at an extreme point of $D$. The conjecture would sharpen the understanding of where Nikol'skii constants attain their maxima; the surrounding discussion notes that boundary maxima are known for several domains, including balls, ellipsoids, cubes, and affine images of cubes, but does not establish the claim for every convex compact domain.
record.source_name: Z. Ditzian and A. Prymak, “On Nikol'skii inequalities for domains in R^d”, arXiv:1409.5397 (2016).
record.references:

record.title: The tightness conjecture for antipodal n-fold covers of spheres
record.statement:
Let $Q(d,n)$ denote the minimum, over antipodal $n$-fold covers of the sphere $S^d$ by open sets, of the maximum number of covering sets containing any point. Theorem~ gives

$$
\left\lceil \frac{d}{2}\right\rceil+n\leq Q(d,n)\leq d+n.
$$

**Tightness conjecture.** For $n\geq 2$,

$$
Q(d,n)=d+n.
$$

The upper bound is attained by Gale's $n$-fold cover, and the conjecture asserts that this construction is optimal for every $n\geq 2$.
record.source_name: Imre Bárány, Ruy Fabila-Monroy and Birgit Vogtenhuber, “(n,m)-Fold Covers of Spheres”, arXiv:1410.0056 (2014).

record.title: Conjectured global supremum for normalized minimal Mahler measure
record.statement:
Let $L(d)$ and $D$ be as above, with $d$ ranging over the relevant square-free positive integers. **Global supremum conjecture.**

$$
\sup_d\frac{L(d)}{\sqrt D}=\frac{L(293)}{\sqrt{293}}=\frac{M\left(\frac{\sqrt{293}+15}{2}\right)}{\sqrt{293}}=\frac{17}{\sqrt{293}}=0.993150\ldots.
$$

The paper says that computations suggest the largest value occurs at $d=293$ and that the upper bound may be slightly reduced; no proof of this exact supremum is supplied.

record.title: Multipartite tiling threshold conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with order $h$ and chromatic number $r$. Let $\chi_{cr}(H)$ denote its critical chromatic number and let $hcf(H)$ denote its highest common factor. For a balanced $r$-partite graph $G$, let $\bar{\delta}(G)$ be its pairwise minimum degree. **Multipartite tiling threshold conjecture.** There exist integers $C$ and $m_0$ such that, for all $m\ge m_0$, if $G$ is a balanced $r$-partite graph with $n=mh$ vertices in each partition set and

$$
\bar{\delta}(G) \ge \begin{cases}
(1-1/\chi_{cr}(H))n+C & \text{if } hcf(H)=1,\\
(1-1/\chi(H))n+C & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
$$

then $G$ contains an $H$-factor. This is proposed as an analogue of the bipartite tiling threshold and the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Albert Bush and Yi Zhao, “Minimum degree thresholds for bipartite graph tiling”, arXiv:1410.4585 (2014).

record.title: The maximal-rank conjecture for regular polytopes with automorphism group \(\mathrm{A}_n\)
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 12$. An abstract regular polytope with automorphism group $\mathrm{A}_n$ has rank $d$, where rank means the number of involutory generators in its string C-group representation. Examples of rank $\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor$ are known. **Maximal-rank conjecture.** The highest rank of an abstract regular polytope having $\mathrm{A}_n$ as automorphism group is

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

This conjecture concerns the largest possible rank of a string C-group representation of the alternating group. The stated lower-bound examples are known, while the conjectured optimality for $n\geq 12$ remains open.
record.source_name: Peter J. Cameron, Maria Elisa Fernandes, Dimitri Leemans and Mark Mixer, “String C-groups as transitive subgroups of Sym(n)”, arXiv:1410.5863 (2014).

record.title: Real-root location conjecture for peak polynomials beyond the final gap
record.statement:
Let $S$ be an admissible peak set with $|S|\ge 2$, and let $S_1$ denote the set obtained by removing the largest element of $S$. Let $p_S(x)$ be the peak polynomial, and let $x_0\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $p_S(x_0)=0$.

**Real-root location conjecture.** The inequality $x_0>\max(S_1)$ holds if and only if

$$
x_0=\max(S).
$$

The conjecture concerns the location of real roots relative to the penultimate peak. The paper proves the assertion for all integer values of $x_0$, but leaves the case of arbitrary real $x_0$ open.
record.source_name: Sara Billey, Matthew Fahrbach and Alan Talmage, “Coefficients and roots of peak polynomials”, arXiv:1410.8506 (2016).

record.title: Proper Hamiltonian cycles in 2-connected edge-colored multigraphs
record.statement:
Let $G^c$ be a $2$-connected $c$-edge-colored multigraph on $n$ vertices, where $n\geq 10$ and $c\geq 3$. Let $rd(G^c)$ denote its rainbow degree and let $m$ be its number of edges. **Proper Hamiltonian cycle conjecture.** If

$$
rd(G^c)=c
$$

and

$$
m\geq c\binom{n-2}{2}+4c+1,
$$

then $G^c$ has a proper Hamiltonian cycle. This conjecture proposes an edge-count condition, together with 2-connectivity and maximum rainbow degree, sufficient to guarantee a proper Hamiltonian cycle in an edge-colored multigraph.
